overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing the 115 Federal Street property at its December 9, 2015 meeting without listing it on the notice; the deliberation and minutes claims failed, and the document and authority claims were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council deliberated outside a noticed meeting in approving the 115 Federal Street property transfer to the PFC.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that a quorum of the Council deliberated outside of a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council discussed the 115 Federal Street property at its December 9, 2015 meeting although the topic was not listed on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: we conclude that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing the 115 Federal Street property during the December 9, 2015 meeting without first including that topic in the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the December 9, 2015 minutes were inaccurate by describing the vote as a transfer to the PFC rather than approval of the MOA.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes accurately reflect the substance of the order executed following the vote, we find that the minutes of the December 19, 2015 meeting are sufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council failed to post or distribute documents used at its 2015 meetings and exceeded its authority in approving the property transfer.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Council's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
